newsitem.title: UK: Cowie hit by British Bus monopoly referral.
newsitem.headline: Cowie hit by British Bus monopoly referral.

text.p: Shares in British vehicle and leasing bus firm Cowie Group tumbled on Thursday after the government said it referred Cowie's acquisition of British Bus Group Ltd to competition authorities.
Cowie shares dropped as low as 337p on the news before recouping losses to trade at 353p by 1144 GMT, down 12p on the day. Over 660,000 shares had changed hands.
The government said it referred the acquisition to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission for investigation because of concerns about bus services in south London and parts of Surrey and Kent.

"It seems unlikely that Cowie would have to divest the whole thing. Reading the statement, it seems the main concerns are with overlap in south London, Surrey and Kent," an analyst at a leading London brokerage said.
"If they were to divest the relevant companies, it would add up to 16 percent of bus company turnover or 70 million stg within group turnover of 1.4 billion," the analyst said.
He noted however that such a divestment might have a greater impact on earnings, accounting for around nine million stg of 107 million annual profit.
The analyst said it was unlikely that the referral would prompt brokers to change recommendations on the stock.
"We would basically have to wait for the MMC's decision before making any moves," he said.
